summary: @qlik/eslint-config-base preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: Package is published as an ESLint config but ships a preinstall script (setup.mjs) that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and uses it to run a bundled 727KB Bun-compiled opaque payload (math_init.js) at install time. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are heavily obfuscated: setup.mjs uses obfuscator.io-style mangled identifiers and string-lookup alias tables; math_init.js contains a shuffled string-array plus rotation function characteristic of javascript-obfuscator output. Neither file is referenced by the ESLint config surface (a ~50-line index.js) and neither is listed in the package.json `files` array (which declares only jest.js, playwright.js, typescript.js, vitest.js). Installing the package causes an alternate-runtime dropper to execute attacker-controlled bytes on the installer's machine before any consumer code runs, giving the publisher arbitrary code execution on every install. The composition (undeclared executables outside the manifest, unrelated Bun runtime pulled for an ESLint config, obfuscated payload) is consistent with a compromise or takeover of the @qlik scope rather than a legitimate release.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
